name: Cream Cheese Pound Cake
desc: Eric Kim's cream cheese pound cake baked in a sheet pan, optionally topped with raspberry jam, salted whipped cream and raspberry dust.

source.title: Cream Cheese Pound Cake
source.evidence: Identical ingredient list and gram weights (320 g flour, 345 g butter, 226 g cream cheese, 600 g sugar, 5 eggs) and the same raspberry, salted cream and freeze-dried raspberry finish in a 9x13 pan at 325°F.

ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups (345 g) unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus more for the pan
ingredients.note: 345 g; plus more for the pan

ingredients.raw: 8 oz (226 g) full-fat cream cheese, at room temperature

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. Butter a 9x13-inch pan and line the bottom and long sides with parchment.
Whisk the flour and baking powder together and set aside.
Beat the butter, cream cheese, sugar, vanilla and salt with a stand mixer on medium-high until fluffy, almost white, and the sugar is mostly dissolved, 5-7 minutes.
On medium speed, add the eggs one at a time, beating until smooth after each. Scrape the bowl and beat 1 minute more.
On low speed, add the flour mixture gradually, mixing only until most streaks are gone, then finish folding by hand with a spatula.
Spread the batter in the pan and smooth the top. Bake 55-65 minutes, rotating halfway, until deep golden, a skewer in the center comes out clean, and a gentle press leaves no dent.
Cool completely in the pan, about 2 hours. Undressed, it keeps covered at room temperature 3 to 4 days.
To finish, spread the preserves over the cooled cake. Whip the cream, sugar and salt to soft, billowy peaks and spread over the jam.
Rub the freeze-dried raspberries through a fine-mesh sieve over the cake until the cream is covered in pink powder. Discard the seeds left in the sieve and serve right away.
tips: NYT Cooking gives 60 to 65 minutes; start checking at 55 because oven and pan color vary.
